Subject: Fall 2027 PhD inquiry: stopping rules for test-time adaptation across hospitals

Dear Professor Raman,

I am a second-year MS student in Computer Science at Northfield University, applying to PhD programs for Fall 2027. I study how segmentation models can adapt safely when deployed at a new hospital.

For my thesis I designed an entropy-based stopping rule for test-time adaptation on cross-site MRI. I wrote the method and ran every experiment; it improved Dice from 0.71 to 0.78 on a held-out site, and the paper is under review at MICCAI.

Your multi-site evaluation protocol separates scanner shift from patient-population shift. My rule fails mainly on the second kind, and your protocol would let me test that directly. I would like to explore whether population shift needs a different adaptation signal altogether.

Will you be advising new PhD students for Fall 2027? I would be glad to talk briefly. My CV is attached; papers are at linchen.github.io.

Best regards,
Lin Chen
